video_title: Inside Gregg Popovich's special bond with Wemby ahead of Spurs-Knicks NBA Finals ❤️ | SportsCenter

quotes.speaker: Victor Wembanyama
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama emphasizes the job is not done yet for the Spurs
quotes.excerpt: we haven't done the hardest yet. The job isn't done at all.
quotes.quote: We still need to really come back down to earth and realize that we haven't done the hardest yet. The job isn't done at all.

quotes.speaker: Devin Vassell
quotes.summary_phrase: Devin Vassell says the Spurs are aiming for an NBA championship
quotes.excerpt: we didn't get here to say we're the Western Conference Finals champions. We want to be NBA champions.
quotes.quote: We are all excited, but we didn't get here to say we're the Western Conference Finals champions. We want to be NBA champions. We won the Finals, so it was great while it lasted, but we're ready for the next chapter.

quotes.speaker: Michael C. Wright
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael C. Wright discusses the Spurs' season of adversity
quotes.excerpt: they've had a bunch of little inflection points throughout the season, and that's been the experience.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael C. Wright
text_blocks.text: Victor Wembanyama said we don't have experience, but we don't care. The Spurs have had a bunch of little inflection points throughout the season, and that's been the experience. They beat the Oklahoma City Thunder three times in 12 days. They go through a winning streak where they win 11 in a row. Then they go up against the New York Knicks and they finally lose. Then you fast forward to the playoffs. Victor Wembanyama face plants, he ends up having to miss that game because he hurt his jaw. Then the next round against Minnesota, he gets suspended for the elbow to Naz Reid. Then they start the Western Conference Finals missing De'Aaron Fox. So they've had little bouts of adversity all season long, and that has been the experience that got them to this stage.

quotes.speaker: Jalen Brunson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson on the Knicks' need to stay focused
quotes.excerpt: our mentality is in the right place at the right time, and we've got to stay focused.
quotes.quote: Our mentality is in the right place at the right time, and we've got to stay focused and keep learning even today. We can't be satisfied just because we're here, we've got to continue to keep learning.

quotes.speaker: Karl-Anthony Towns
quotes.summary_phrase: Karl-Anthony Towns on the Knicks tapping into their collective experience
quotes.excerpt: all of us are going to have to tap into that reserve of experience.
quotes.quote: All of us are going to have to tap into that reserve of experience, whether it's Jalen with winning in college and winning a national championship, or with me personally with the failures I have in my career with not getting to the Finals or in college not winning at all. We all got to tap into that experience we have so we can put ourselves in the best chance and the best position to win.

quotes.speaker: Vincent Goodwill
quotes.summary_phrase: Vincent Goodwill on Stephon Castle's defensive impact on Jalen Brunson
quotes.excerpt: on the 11 shots that Jalen Brunson has played against Stephon Castle, he's three of 11.
quotes.quote: Jalen Brunson has made note of how great of a defender Stephon Castle is. He said I've been paying attention to him since he was at UConn. He called him tenacious. On the 11 shots that Jalen Brunson has played against Stephon Castle, he's three of 11, that's 27 percent. That's a pretty low number for someone as efficient as Jalen Brunson. We've seen it from Stephon Castle from guarding Anthony Edwards and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and also Julius Randle, he's going to spend a lot of time on the Knicks' top scorer.

quotes.speaker: Vincent Goodwill
quotes.summary_phrase: Vincent Goodwill on the difficulty of stopping Victor Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: you can get yourself in a lot of trouble if you pay attention to just Victor.
quotes.quote: You ask Josh Hart about it and he said look, there's no way to prepare for this guy. There's no player that is like him. But he also said there's no way that you can just focus on Victor Wembanyama. You can get yourself in a lot of trouble if you pay attention to just Victor and not the Stephon Castles and Julian Champagnies who were really, really hot towards the second half of that series against Oklahoma City.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Gregg Popovich's emotional impact on Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: the honesty that we saw from Victor there, talking about how emotional he was talking to Greg Popovich.
quotes.quote: The honesty that we saw from Victor there, talking about how emotional he was talking to Greg Popovich, and it multiple times during this postseason, when he dealt with the concussion in round one, when he got ejected and his team lost in round two to Minnesota, Greg Popovich met him at the airport. When the team got behind in the conference finals 2-1, Greg Popovich was there talking to the team. There he is, Greg Popovich again, when they come back from Oklahoma City to handle the emotion and get them refocused on the Finals. Obviously, Greg Popovich has been around this team a lot. He's been around Victor a lot since he arrived here in San Antonio three years ago, but the role that he has played as El Jefe, as they call him around here, in this postseason has really been valuable.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the Spurs' defensive strategy against the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: the Spurs go conventional, and what that means against the Knicks is putting Victor Wembanyama on Josh Hart.
quotes.quote: The Spurs go conventional, and what that means against the Knicks is putting Victor Wembanyama on Josh Hart, backing off of him on the perimeter, and sitting in the lane so he can defend Jalen Brunson drives. Now, Josh Hart at times in this postseason has destroyed this strategy. I'll just use the word analytically, and then you can go from there. There's been other times when it's been such an effective strategy that Josh Hart has been benched. He's only shooting 30 percent on threes in the series, and that is where the rubber is going to meet the road in terms of going into the Game 1 strategy.
